q: How many more clips did the horseshoe hold than the small bar magnet?
Explain why counting paper clips is a fair way to compare magnets, and name one control variable.
More clips held means a stronger magnetic force. Control: the same type and size of paper clip, hung from the same end (pole).
A student says the large bar magnet is stronger than the small one "because it is bigger". Evaluate this using the data.
The large bar held more (9 vs 6), so the data supports it for these two; but the small neodymium magnet held the most (18), so size alone does not decide strength: the material matters.
